messages:
alyssa: Quick thread — I'm seeing a consistent tail-latency regression when we enable per-channel FP8 calibration on the 70B runtime in the kv-cache heavy workload. Results from yesterday's canary: 95th went from 210ms -> 310ms for small batch sizes. Anyone else?
kevin: ugh that's bad. is it only with per-channel? what about per-tensor?
maria: confirmed on my end with a /trace run. per-channel gives slightly better avg perplexity but latency tails blow up under hotkey traffic. appears during KV cache warmup spikes.
samir: do you have the profile? can you paste the hot path? :eyes:
alyssa: pasted below — it's the canary run for region-us-east, model variant fp8-per-channel. interestingly the slow frames are on the attention kernel selection path where we recompile/choose fallback kernels when quant bias exceeds threshold.

```# perf snippet (trimmed)
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] dispatch: select_kernel(attn, seq=128) -> kernel_fp8_mixed_opt
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] kv: cache_miss -> warmup_copy
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] kernel_exec: attn_fp8_fallback (20ms) vs attn_fp8_opt (6ms)
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] route: fallback due to per-channel scale variance > 0.12
```

kevin: so fallback kernels are being chosen mid-flight because calibration produced per-channel scales with larger spread?
maria: my hypothesis: per-channel calibration with outliers in dataset skews some channel scales, which trips the runtime's stability heuristic and causes fallback to slower kernels. per-tensor is more conservative and avoids that, at cost of small accuracy drop.
jess: what was the calibration dataset here? did it include very long docs or code-heavy samples? those create extreme attention patterns which can produce outliers.
alyssa: config was: 5k prompts sampled from prod, sampled uniformly across customers. We didn't clip on sequence length or remove hotkey-heavy sessions. sample config: 

```
calib: { "mode": "per-channel", "num_samples": 5000, "max_seq": 2048, "filter": "none" }
```

samir: that's the issue then — uniform sampling pulls in hotkey-heavy traffic (many repeated prefixes), which over-represents rare tokens and creates per-channel scale outliers. We should try: 1) sequence-length stratification, 2) percentile clipping on per-channel scales, 3) a small holdout set with typical request distribution.
kevin: can we reproduce locally with a smaller sample? maybe 512 prompts stratified? would like a quick A/B.
maria: yes, I ran 512 stratified by seq buckets (<=64, 65-512, 513-2048) and per-channel still had a couple of channels with scale > 0.2 while per-tensor kept scale ~0.05. When I applied 99.9th percentile clipping on per-channel scales, the runtime no longer triggered fallback and 95th latency returned to ~220ms.
jess: interesting — how did accuracy change after clipping? any eval deltas?
maria: small delta: +0.3 ppl on long-form eval, negligible on chat eval. Tradeoff seems acceptable for production SLOs.
alyssa: question: should our recommended default be per-tensor calibration for public hosted, and per-channel only with an outlier handling step? or keep per-channel but add auto-clipping?
samir: prefer keep per-channel as opt-in for teams needing best quality. But we should implement auto-clipping heuristic in the quant pipeline and surface a warning in the console when per-channel scale variance is high. Also add an option: `clip_percentile: 99.5` and `exclude_hotkeys: true` for sample selection.
kevin: operationally, enabling clip_percentile by default for per-channel makes sense. Need a regression test to catch kernel fallback events. perf-bot can monitor kernel choice distributions in canaries.
perf-bot: regression alert: canary 2026-03-15-03 detected kernel fallback rate increase -> +14% relative; triggered paging threshold.
jess: nice — we can add a unit test in calib-suite: synthesize a few prompts with extreme token frequency and ensure per-channel scales are clipped. Also add end-to-end smoke that checks 95th latency on kv-heavy traces.
alyssa: next steps: maria to run experiments with `clip_percentile` {99.0, 99.5, 99.9} on the 5k uniform vs stratified 512; samir to PR a runtime guard that logs kernel selection cause; kevin to add perf-bot kernel-fallback monitor. I'll compile results and propose default flags.
maria: started runs now, ETA ~2 hours. will paste summary.
samir: I'll create the runtime log metric: `kernel_fallback_rate` and tag by calib-mode.
kevin: can we also record `kv_warmup_miss_rate` in the same traces? looks correlated.
maria: added that metric to the experiment. preliminary: clip 99.5 reduces fallback by ~80% and brings 95th within 10% of baseline.
jess: :thumbsup: sounds like a plan.
alyssa: thanks all — this was a good find. we'll follow up with a short RFC for calibration defaults and a console warning.
perf-bot: note: scheduled canary rollout paused until kernel_fallback_rate < threshold.
